history.rationale: Arg157 lies in the strictly conserved ALRGD motif of the FAD-binding TIM-barrel and is a documented severe MTHFR-deficiency allele that destabilizes FAD binding. Loss of the FAD cofactor should essentially abolish catalytic activity while the protein still folds.

Thr227 is in the conserved 'ITQ(L)FF' barrel strand of the catalytic domain; T227M is a classic severe loss-of-function MTHFR-deficiency mutation. The bulky Met is predicted to disrupt active-site packing and folate/FAD geometry.

Asp159 corresponds to E. coli MetF Asp120, a catalytic/FAD-proximal carboxylate whose neutralization abolishes turnover. The conservative D->N change should retain folding while removing the essential charge.

Glu63 in the invariant EFFPPRT motif aligns with MetF Glu28, the proposed catalytic acid/base near FAD N5. Isosteric neutralization to Gln should eliminate proton transfer without gross structural collapse.

Gly158 sits in the tight ALRGD turn that cradles the FAD isoalloxazine; only glycine is tolerated at this backbone conformation. Introducing a large charged Arg should sterically and electrostatically block cofactor binding.

Leu156 is a buried hydrophobic residue immediately preceding the catalytic ALRGD arginine; proline would break the local secondary structure and backbone hydrogen bonding. Expected to destroy active-site architecture.

Tyr321 is part of the highly conserved HFYTLNRE motif implicated in folate/methyl-transfer chemistry in MetF homologs. Replacing a buried aromatic with Asp should abolish substrate binding and catalysis.
Arg68 in the invariant EFFPPRT loop is positioned to contact the FAD pyrophosphate; charge reversal should repel the cofactor. Predicted strong loss of activity with modest folding penalty.
Tyr197 in the conserved AGYPKGHPEA loop corresponds to MetF Tyr(AAYPEVHPE), a residue lining the FAD/folate pocket. A buried-to-charged substitution should disrupt cofactor stacking and catalysis.

A222V is the well-known C677T thermolabile variant that lowers activity and promotes FAD loss, so directionality toward loss-of-function is well established. Confidence is limited because it reduces rather than fully abolishes activity.
